### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/spec`, touching **38** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/dropped-refinements.baseline.json`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**77** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 738971d2eabaaa677b894ae6030cac5b887f9bc6`.

⛔ **17** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/dropped-refinements.baseline.json`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `defaultValue (literal, 41 pages)`
- **12** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **60** of **216** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **156** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **156**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **101** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **168** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 738971d2eabaaa677b894ae6030cac5b887f9bc6` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `ec41b2be516ea3244a9947b137535dacfc87187b` — the merge of head `5f8d7494c93b397f54abc4deeea5780025d4335d` into base `738971d2eabaaa677b894ae6030cac5b887f9bc6`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin ec41b2be516ea3244a9947b137535dacfc87187b && git checkout ec41b2be516ea3244a9947b137535dacfc87187b
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 738971d2eabaaa677b894ae6030cac5b887f9bc6 5f8d7494c93b397f54abc4deeea5780025d4335d && git checkout -B drift-repro 738971d2eabaaa677b894ae6030cac5b887f9bc6 && git merge --no-ff 5f8d7494c93b397f54abc4deeea5780025d4335d

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 738971d2eabaaa677b894ae6030cac5b887f9bc6
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 738971d2eabaaa677b894ae6030cac5b887f9bc6` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## 席位核对 — ACCEPT · `domain:spec#1` · head `5f8d7494`

1. **Shape:** draft, base `main`, `Fixes #28655`, `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` / `Metadata-protocol: narrowed` at line start in the body and the changeset (BREAKING spec minor). Surface: claim 6574981251 as amended on #28655 (field.zod.ts, the new leaf `data/field-key-aliases.ts`, one docs bullet, the options-map proto guard). Not governed.
2. **Diff, read on the head:** A, the root `superRefine` refuses a field that is both in `fields` and in `fieldPatches` (custom issue at `fieldPatches.NAME`; a `__c` name is left to the `__c` rule). B, a field patch's `options` map is keyed by `SelectOptionSchema.shape.value` (`invalid_key` with a prescription), and `refuseRecordProtoKey` guards `fields`, `fieldPatches` and the `options` map. C, both patch surfaces carry the rename guidance the whitelist admits, from the shared leaf, which `FieldSchema` and `SelectOptionSchema` now read too (rows byte-identical; no barrel export). D, the `fieldPatches` describe is built from `BASE_FIELD_DISPLAY_WHITELIST`. `dropped-refinements.baseline.json`: five `fields.valueType` sites moved to `fields.out.valueType` (the guard's preprocess), no new site.
3. **Premise, re-measured by the dev:** `mergeObjectDefinitions` applies `fieldPatches` on main; in-repo authored A/B hits are 0 (examples, skills, docs). The `__proto__` loss was measured at the `/meta` save door on main. HotCRM was not measured (not reachable from the container). The seat accepts that risk for landing: every refused form fails at `os validate` / save with a named prescription (rename the patch, drop the duplicate, re-key the option), nothing is dropped in silence, and this repo's examples, skills and docs carry zero refused forms.
4. **Tests:** +130 / +19 new; six ablation legs, each red on its own pin. No forced test edits.
5. **Readings (dev, on `5f8d7494`):** 103/103 derived gates, DERIVED zero; dogfood 389 files / 3215 tests green; spec 790 files; objectql, metadata-protocol, metadata-core, lint, cloud-connection, rest and cli consumer suites green. `main` moved to `192c15cf` after the round with no overlapping path, and the PR's CI runs on the merge ref. Check-runs on `5f8d7494` at this reading: 57 success, 8 skipped, 0 failure, 0 running.
6. **Landing:** one `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` review (a narrowing on the published schema face), which the seat runs itself (claim line follows). Then the seat readies and queues. After it lands, #29171 (same file) and #28205 / #29007 (`object.zod.ts`) are next.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `5f8d7494c93b397f54abc4deeea5780025d4335d`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/data/field-key-aliases.ts, packages/spec/src/data/field.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/data/object.zod.ts + packages/objectql/src/registry.ts (`mergeObjectDefinitions`, `applyFieldPatches`, `patchedField`, `ownFieldNamesOf`), packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-object-extension-item.ts (`OBJECT_EXTENSION_ITEM_SCHEMA`, `registrableObjectExtension`), packages/objectql/src/engine.ts (the `objectExtensions` registration loop), packages/spec/src/shared/record-proto-key-guard.ts (`refuseRecordProtoKey`), packages/spec/src/shared/strict-object.ts (`aliases` semantics), packages/spec/src/shared/identifiers.zod.ts (`SystemIdentifierSchema`), packages/spec/src/data/field-customization.ts (`BASE_FIELD_DISPLAY_WHITELIST`, `isExtensionFieldName`), packages/spec/src/data/authoring-key-lint.ts (`FIELD_KEY_GUIDANCE`), packages/spec/src/shared/suggestions.zod.ts (import graph), packages/spec/src/shared/alias-integrity.test.ts (the invariants the new tables must hold), packages/spec/src/data/index.ts and packages/spec/package.json `exports` (public-name question), packages/spec/dropped-refinements.baseline.json, packages/spec/src/data/field-customization.test.ts, packages/spec/src/data/field-patches-derived.test.ts, .changeset/28655-field-patches-refuse-replaced-field.md, content/docs/data-modeling/object-extensions.mdx, content/docs/references/data/object.mdx, skills/objectstack-data/SKILL.md, docs/adr/0146-studio-designs-setup-administers-one-editor-per-item-paired-customize-package.md (D10), scripts/check-adr-0087-registration.mjs (the `no-migration-prescription` rule). Every non-prose path of the diff is inside this list (narrowing face: no remainder).

Face: schema (`reviewFace` hits the three `packages/spec/src/data` paths) and a declared narrowing (`Clause-②: no (narrowing)` on the PR body and the changeset). Inputs read: card #28655 body and all four comments (triage 6561051425 and 6572269927, claim 6574981251, dev report 6576784326 — the seat's claim amendment widening the surface to `field.zod.ts`, the new leaf, one docs bullet and the options-map proto guard is taken as accepted surface), PR #29331 body, file list and net diff against `main` (merge base `47ee57fe`), and the check-runs on this head.

Gate verdicts on `5f8d7494`, read off the check-runs: Lint & Repo Gates success · TypeScript Type Check success · Test Core success · Build Core success · Governed Surface Queue Guard success · Type Check UI success · Test UI success · Build & E2E UI success · Live E2E UI success · Lint UI skipped (path-filtered; no `ui/` path in the diff) · Check Changeset success · Spec property liveness success · PR-body guards success · Dogfood Regression Gate success. No required context red or in progress.

### ① Derived judgments

Each judgment is read off the tree at the head, never off the PR body.

- **A — refuse a field both in `fields` and `fieldPatches` of one extension: RIGHT.** `refuseFieldPatchOfReplacedField` runs in `ObjectExtensionSchema`'s root `superRefine`, walks `Object.keys(fieldPatches)` and refuses every key that is an own key of `fields`, `custom` at `fieldPatches.NAME`, skipping a `__c` name (left to `refuseExtensionFieldPatchKeys`, so it is refused once). Accept-set change: the pair {same record key in both maps} leaves the accept set; nothing else moves. The record key is the only spelling that matters: `mergeObjectDefinitions` merges `fields` by key (`{ ...base.fields, ...extension.fields }`) and `applyFieldPatches` addresses the field by key, `FieldSchema.name` is optional and the engine's `objectExtensions` loop re-keys nothing (it hands `ext.fields` through), so a patch and a replacement collide exactly when their record keys are equal — which is the predicate the refinement tests. Measured against the merge: for an owner-declared `industry` replaced in `fields`, `ownFields` contains `industry`, so the patch was written onto `merged.fields.industry`, the extension's replacement — the defect the card names is real on `main` and is closed here.
- **B (key) — key the `options` map by `SelectOptionSchema.shape.value`: RIGHT.** The key schema is the very instance `SelectOptionSchema` declares for `value` (`SystemIdentifierSchema.describe(...)`: `min(2)`, `/^[a-z][a-z0-9_.]*$/`), read off the shape, not restated. `FieldSchema.options` is `z.array(SelectOptionSchema)`, so no option an owner can declare carries a value this key refuses; the one other option shape with a looser `value` (the inline-grid column's) is not a field's options and is not patchable. A picklist-bound field is skipped by `patchedField` anyway. Accept-set change: an option-patch key outside the value grammar (`Tech Sector`, `2nd`, `x`) leaves the accept set with `invalid_key` at `fieldPatches.F.options.K` and a message naming the grammar.
- **B (proto) — refuse `__proto__` on the raw input of `fields`, `fieldPatches` and each `options` map: RIGHT.** `refuseRecordProtoKey` is the pre-parse `z.preprocess` guard `ObjectSchema.fields` already carries (zod 4.4.3's record parser `continue`s on `__proto__` above the key schema, so no key schema — B's included — can see it). The three record slots are the only maps `ObjectExtensionSchema` declares (`validations` and `indexes` are arrays), so no map is left unguarded. The `/api/v1/meta` save door and the sync both parse `OBJECT_EXTENSION_ITEM_SCHEMA = z.preprocess(withoutProtectionEnvelope, ObjectExtensionSchema)`, so the refusal is the door's and the sync's, not only the schema's. `constructor` / `prototype` are deliberately outside the guard (its docblock), and this diff does not change their accept status on the extension — unchanged, not a regression.
- **C — carry the whitelisted rename rows onto both patch surfaces: RIGHT, and it widens nothing.** `strictObject`'s `aliases` are consulted only on the `unrecognized_keys` path (`strict-object.ts`: "an alias runs only from the `unrecognized_keys` path") — a hint appended to a refusal, never a rewrite — so every key C touches was refused before and is refused after; only the message changes. `whitelistedAliases` keeps the rows whose TARGET is in `BASE_FIELD_DISPLAY_WHITELIST.field` / `.option`: on the field patch `title`, `displayName` → `label` and `help`, `helpText`, `hint`, `tooltip` → `inlineHelpText` (`FIELD_KEY_GUIDANCE` carries no `to:` onto any admitted target — grepped — so those six rows are the whole carried set); on the option patch `text`, `name`, `title` → `label`. The alias-integrity invariants hold on both tables by construction: no carried alias key is a declared patch key (none was a declared `FieldSchema` / `SelectOptionSchema` key either), every target is a key the patch accepts, and no two keys collapse onto one probe (they did not on the source tables). `displayName` beyond the card's list is a correct consequence of the filter, pinned.
- **D — describe built from the constant: RIGHT.** `fieldPatchesDescription()` reads `BASE_FIELD_DISPLAY_WHITELIST.field` and `.option` through `backtickList`; the sentence keeps `mergeObjectDefinitions` (the existing liveness pin) and gains "a field the same extension replaces in `fields` is refused here"; `content/docs/references/data/object.mdx` is the regenerated projection of exactly that string. Emission change on the published description only; no accept-set change.
- **The `field.zod.ts` move changes nothing `FieldSchema` / `SelectOptionSchema` accept or emit: RIGHT.** Set-compared: the 61 rows removed from `FieldSchema`'s inline `aliases` equal `FIELD_ALIAS_ROWS`, the 10 rows removed from `SelectOptionSchema`'s inline `aliases` equal `SELECT_OPTION_ALIASES`; precedence is preserved (`{ ...fieldKeyGuidanceAsStrictOptions().aliases, ...FIELD_ALIAS_ROWS }` as before, own rows winning); `guidance` still spreads `fieldKeyGuidanceAsStrictOptions().guidance`; both reads stay inside `lazySchema` bodies as before. Aliases are hint-only (above), so even a row drift would not have moved the accept set — and there is none.
- **Public surface and import graph: RIGHT, no new public name, no cycle.** `field-key-aliases.ts` is not exported from `data/index.ts`, and `packages/spec/package.json` `exports` are fixed subpaths (no wildcard), so the leaf is reachable by relative import only — the `ui/action-target-aliases.ts` precedent; `api-surface/` is untouched and `check:api-surface` is green. Edges added: `object.zod → field-key-aliases → authoring-key-lint → suggestions.zod`; `suggestions.zod` at this head imports `protocol-upgrade-guide`, `alias-probe` and `polarity-axes` only, and `field.zod → authoring-key-lint` already existed, so no cycle is introduced. The leaf's module scope holds two literals and two function declarations, so eager-schema load order cannot bite it.
- **`dropped-refinements.baseline.json`: RIGHT.** The five `data/ObjectExtension` sites move from `fields.valueType…` to `fields.out.valueType…` — the convention the baseline already uses for the guarded `ObjectSchema.fields` (`manifest.objects.element.fields.out.valueType`) — because the guard is a preprocess pipe; same five sites, one level deeper, no site added, no site dropped. `fieldPatches` and its `options` carry no refinement, so wrapping them adds no site; the gate is green.

### ② Semver level

- `.changeset/28655-field-patches-refuse-replaced-field.md`: `'@objectstack/spec': minor` with a `feat(spec)!:` headline, a **BREAKING** accept-set-narrowing banner, Before / Now / Unchanged / Who-sees-it and a remedy. Line-initial `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` and `Metadata-protocol: narrowed`, the same two lines on the PR body. A kind takes at least `minor` on the package the diff moves; `(narrowing)` is the BREAKING arm — the level matches what the diff publishes (three refusals on `ObjectExtensionSchema`, nothing widened, no key added, removed or renamed, no export changed).
- ADR-0087 marker: exactly one, `not-required (no-migration-prescription)`. Right in substance: no authorable key is added, removed or renamed, so there is nothing for `objectstack migrate meta` or a conversion-layer entry to rewrite — a field both replaced and patched carries two opposite intents and no rewrite keeps both, an option key outside the value grammar never addressed an option (mapping a label to a value needs the target's options, which the schema does not have), and `__proto__` has no successor key. The remedy in the body is a decision the author makes per field, not a FROM → TO rewrite; the gate that re-validates this disposition statement-against-statement (`check:adr-0087-registration`, inside Lint & Repo Gates) is green on this head.
- Changelog / releases untouched; the `content/docs/references/` edit is the generator's output (`check:docs` green). Human Minimum item 5 holds.

### ③ Boundary flags

The dev report names six deviations; each answered here.

1. **File surface widened** (`field.zod.ts`, the new leaf `data/field-key-aliases.ts`, one bullet in `content/docs/data-modeling/object-extensions.mdx`): accepted — the seat's claim amendment covers exactly these, and the move is the mechanism C needs (one table, two readers; exporting it from `field.zod.ts` would have ridden the `data` barrel into the published API). Answered.
2. **Options-map `__proto__` guard beyond the card's `fields` and `fieldPatches`**: accepted by the same amendment, and necessary rather than extra — zod skips `__proto__` above the key schema, so without it B's key grammar could never see that key. Same defect class, same wrapper, same schema. Answered.
3. **Baseline sites moved to `fields.out.*`**: a consequence of the preprocess, matching the convention already in the file; no new site. Answered (①). Note for the landing: `main` has since moved the same file in a disjoint block (`ui/Dashboard` gains one site; `droppedRefinementSites` 983 → 988); the hunks do not overlap and this PR adds no site, so the text merge is the right merge — the baseline is `NOT_DRIVER_MANAGED`, so the seat reads that conflict-free merge rather than regenerating.
4. **`main` moved after the verification round; no merge before `pr_create`**: the PR's check-runs ran on the merge ref and are green; on the three `hits` paths `main` has not moved since the merge base (`git diff --stat 47ee57fe origin/main` on them: nothing), only the baseline (point 3). Answered.
5. **No PR assignee / reviewer**: `.claude/agents/os-dev.md` says `pr_create` carries no `assignees`, while AGENTS.md (which wins on conflict) says the PR's assignee mirrors the card's, set by the executor at `pr_create`. Not a contract finding on this diff; **escalated to the seat** as an instruction inconsistency on a Tier S surface (`.claude/**`) to reconcile on its own card. No effect on this verdict.
6. **HotCRM fixtures NOT MEASURED** (repository not reachable from the dev's container): the refusals are correct on this tree whatever HotCRM carries, and in this repository `examples/`, `skills/` and `content/docs/` hold zero refused forms (re-read: the only authored `fieldPatches` key options by `technology`). **Escalated to the seat**: before landing a BREAKING narrowing, take the HotCRM reading (count of extensions naming one field in both maps, or keying an option patch by a non-grammar string) or record the acceptance of the unmeasured risk on the card. No effect on this verdict.

### ④ Design judgment

Judged on the tree, file by file, against the code each hunk cites.

**`packages/spec/src/data/object.zod.ts`**

- *Does A fire on every spelling a field can be both replaced and patched?* Yes within one extension: the collision the merge produces is key-equality on the two records, and that is what the refinement tests (`Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call(fields, name)` over `Object.keys(fieldPatches)`). Tried to break it: a `fields` entry whose `.name` differs from its key does not collide in the merge (key-based), so there is nothing to refuse; a `__c` key is refused once by the sibling rule, with a prescription that already names `fields`; a non-object `fields` or `fieldPatches` returns early, and the shape has already refused it. One ordering fact, not a defect: the root `superRefine` runs only once every nested property parsed (zod 4 skips a schema's checks on an aborted payload), so an extension whose `fields.industry` is itself invalid sees A only after that field parses — the same ordering the existing `__c` rule has. Observation outside the card (not a finding on this PR): across TWO extensions, a lower-priority extension that replaces `industry` in `fields` and a higher one that patches it still land the patch on the replacement (`mergeObjectDefinitions` applies each contributor's patches onto the running `merged.fields`); that is `main`'s documented priority semantics, not this card's, and is noted for the lane.
- *Can B's key schema refuse a value `SelectOptionSchema` accepts?* No: it is the same schema instance (`optionShape.value`), and every option an owner's field declares is a `SelectOptionSchema` (`FieldSchema.options: z.array(SelectOptionSchema)`), so key grammar and value grammar cannot diverge. The `error` map keeps the array-shaped `invalid_type` prescription and adds the `invalid_key` one; the control pin asserts key verdict equals `SelectOptionSchema.shape.value.safeParse` on four spellings.
- *Does the proto guard leave any map unguarded?* No — `fields`, `fieldPatches` and `fieldPatches.*.options` are the three records the extension declares and all three are wrapped; the guard is placed inside `.optional().describe()` so the clone-safe `optin` patch in `refuseProtoOwnKey` holds, and the issue paths (`fields.__proto__`, `fieldPatches.__proto__`, `fieldPatches.F.options.__proto__`) are pinned over JSON documents, the shape the save door receives.
- *C on this file:* `whitelistedAliases` filters by TARGET against `admitted`, so a row onto a refused key (`isRequired` → `required`, `key` → `value`) is not carried — the alias-integrity invariant "every alias target is a key the schema accepts" holds. Deliberate and accepted: rows onto `options` (`values`, `choices`, `selectOptions`) are not carried either, because the patch's `options` is a map of patches, not the field's option list a rename would imply. The `guidanceSets` structural keys and the carried alias keys are disjoint (no alias key is a `FieldSchema` key).
- *D on this file:* `fieldPatchesDescription()` and `fieldPatchStructuralPrescription()` now read the same constant; the mocked-whitelist pin proves widening reaches the description.
- **Should-fix (non-blocking, a follow-up card):** `fieldPatches`' own key stays `z.string()` while a field name has a grammar (`FieldSchema.name` `/^[a-z_][a-z0-9_]*$/`, and `ObjectSchema.fields` keys are snake_case), so `fieldPatches: { Industry: { label: 'Sector' } }` still parses and is refused only downstream by the target judge (install door, `os validate`, boot log). Same class as B, same derivation available (read the key schema off `ObjectSchema.fields`), outside the card's four items. Not a FAIL.

**`packages/spec/src/data/field-key-aliases.ts`**

- *Does moving the tables into a relative-import-only leaf create a public name or an import cycle?* No public name: not in the `data` barrel, no wildcard subpath in `exports`, `api-surface/` unchanged. No cycle: the leaf imports only `./authoring-key-lint`, whose transitive imports (`suggestions.zod` → `protocol-upgrade-guide`, `alias-probe`, `polarity-axes`) do not reach `field.zod` or `object.zod` at this head; `fieldSchemaAliases()` is a function for the reason its docblock gives and both consumers call it inside `lazySchema` bodies. The exported `fieldKeyGuidanceAsStrictOptions` is the former module-private function, still reached only by `field.zod.ts`. Row-identical to the inline tables it replaces (set-compared, 61 and 10 rows). Holds.
